title: Cardiac tamponade after cardiac surgery and in trauma
subtitle: Recognise it, open the chest early, avoid the induction trap

sources.title: Guideline for resuscitation in cardiac arrest after cardiac surgery
The STS Expert Consensus for the Resuscitation of Patients Who Arrest After Cardiac Surgery
European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2021: Cardiac arrest in special circumstances
2015 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of pericardial diseases

red_flags.text: After cardiac surgery: falling cardiac output, rising filling pressures, rising inotrope need, falling urine output, and chest drain output that suddenly stops after being heavy.
Equalisation of filling pressures, pulsus paradoxus, or a narrowing pulse pressure in a patient after cardiac surgery.
Late tamponade days after surgery, often on anticoagulation, presenting as breathlessness, low output or hypotension. It may be localised clot, not a circumferential effusion.
Penetrating wound to the precordium or epigastrium with hypotension: tamponade until proven otherwise. Distended neck veins may be absent if hypovolaemic.
Pulseless electrical activity in any of these patients.

do_now.text: Arrest after cardiac surgery: in VF or pulseless VT, give up to three quick successive shocks before starting external compressions.
Arrest after cardiac surgery that does not respond to initial measures: emergency resternotomy within about 5 minutes, by a team trained to do it.
Do not give routine full-dose adrenaline in arrest after cardiac surgery. It can cause severe rebound hypertension and bleeding once output returns.
Traumatic tamponade in a peri-arrest patient: release the pericardium surgically by thoracotomy or sternotomy. Needle pericardiocentesis is a bridge at best because the blood is clotted.

assess.text: Beck triad (hypotension, raised venous pressure, muffled heart sounds) is incomplete in most patients. Do not wait for all three.
After cardiac surgery, check drain patency, the trend in drain output, mixed venous saturation, and the response of pressure to fluid.
Pacing wires: check the pacing mode and capture in a bradycardic or asystolic arrest after cardiac surgery.
Trauma: wound location, eFAST pericardial view, and response to fluid.

investigate.text: Transthoracic echocardiography first; transoesophageal echocardiography after cardiac surgery when windows are poor or localised clot is suspected.
eFAST in trauma. A negative pericardial view with a large haemothorax can be falsely negative because blood decompresses into the pleura.
Chest radiograph for mediastinal widening and drain position; coagulation, platelets and fibrinogen after cardiac surgery.

resuscitate.text: Give volume to maintain preload while the definitive release is arranged. Avoid vasodilators and high intrathoracic pressures.
Prepare and drape the chest before induction of anaesthesia for surgical drainage. Induction and positive pressure ventilation can cause collapse.
After cardiac surgery, correct coagulopathy and treat bleeding per the unit protocol while preparing for re-exploration.

definitive.text: Tamponade after cardiac surgery: surgical re-exploration through the sternotomy, evacuation of clot and control of bleeding.
Medical or late post-operative effusion with tamponade: echocardiography-guided pericardiocentesis, or surgical drainage when the fluid is clotted, localised or recurrent.
Traumatic tamponade: pericardiotomy and repair of the cardiac wound via sternotomy, or left anterolateral or clamshell thoracotomy in the arrested patient.
Aortic dissection with haemopericardium: surgical repair. Pericardiocentesis risks further bleeding and is reserved for the patient who cannot otherwise reach theatre.

escalate.text: Cardiac surgeon immediately for any suspected tamponade after cardiac surgery, day or night.
In trauma, the trauma surgeon and cardiothoracic surgeon together; transfer only when the pericardium is already decompressed or the patient is stable.
Cardiac anaesthetist for induction. This is one of the most dangerous inductions in medicine.

notes: After cardiac surgery a drain that suddenly stops is more often clotted than dry.
Tamponade is a diagnosis of physiology. Echo confirms it, but a dying patient after cardiac surgery is opened, not scanned.
In traumatic tamponade the blood is clot. A needle rarely removes enough of it, and a scalpel does.
